text: This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.

"What is burning?" — the wood burns because of the fire, the fire burns because of the wood. This itself shows idappaccayata — this happens because that happened. The fire simile has very deep significance. Upadana — holding on — means BOTH fuel and holding on. The fire grasps the wood, the wood grasps the fire. We call it "firewood."
destruction alone is not Nibbana — out, like a flame with no fuel. Nanananda — this is a commentarial invention, not a sutta position.

That form by which one designating the Tathagata might designate him, that has been abandoned by him, cut off at the root, made like an uprooted palm tree. The Tathagata is past all counting in terms of form, so deep you cannot measure it, like the great ocean.
It can in no way be compared to going out, like a flame with no fuel and the cooling down of the Arahants.

This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.

One who has quenched his wanting for good is aware of that blissful experience. When he sees the world running here and there in search of water, he looks within and sees the well-spring of his bliss.

This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.

Sa-upadisesa — with fuel still left — — the arahant is free from fresh holding on, lust, hate and delusions do not flare up. But so long as he has to bear the burden of this organic combination, the arahant has to experience certain afflictions.

When he feels a pleasant-or-unpleasant tone limited to the body, he understands 'I feel a pleasant-or-unpleasant tone limited to the body'... he understands 'on the breaking up of this body, before life becomes extinct, even here itself, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool'.
This is the highest knowledge, this is the unsurpassed bliss, this sorrow-less, taintless security, is the supreme debtless-ness.

Samsara or reiterated existence is itself a debt, which one can never pay off. When one comes to think of kamma — what you do and what comes back — and its result, it is a debt that keeps on gathering an interminable interest.. Even from this debt the arahants have won freedom by destroying the seeds of kamma — what you do and what comes back —, by rendering them infertile.
